name: Phil Spector
hook: A producer who treated the pop single as a wall of sound built from dozens of musicians, whose method Brian Wilson built Pet Sounds on, and who was convicted of murder in 2009.
blurb: Phil Spector was born in the Bronx in 1939. In late 1961 he co-founded his own label, Philles Records, with Lester Sill. He made hit singles like the Ronettes' 'Be My Baby' (1963), which reached number two, by filling Gold Star Studios in Hollywood with the session players later called the Wrecking Crew: several guitars, pianos and percussionists all playing the same parts at once, then drowned in reverb and echo and mixed for mono and AM radio. People called it the Wall of Sound. Brian Wilson of the Beach Boys built his records on it. Spector was later brought in to finish the Beatles' abandoned 'Let It Be' sessions (1970), adding orchestral parts that Paul McCartney objected to, and he produced the Ramones' 'End of the Century' (1980). How he behaved in the studio, including accounts of guns at sessions, is disputed in detail by the musicians who were there, and is stated on the connections where it is sourced. In 2009 he was convicted of the second-degree murder of the actress Lana Clarkson, who was killed at his house on 3 February 2003, and sentenced to 19 years to life. He died in prison in 2021.
